note: Merged from eight batch files; two batches interrupted by a usage limit were finished by further independent agents with the same instructions (part names record which).

scores.notes: The two seraphim (upper center) each have only two wings, are veiled by cloth hoods rather than wings, and show bare exposed feet, contradicting the verse's six wings covering face and feet; the right seraph also holds tongs with a burning coal (the later v6 action). God appears only as glow and smoke over the sanctuary, and all four edges are painted with no lettering.

Bearded Ezekiel in a rough cloak stands center-left among skulls and skeletons, one hand outstretched toward the bones. He holds a blank wooden tablet and stylus (not requested, no marks on it). God appears nowhere, and the light strokes in the bottom-right corner are a dry grass tuft, not letters.

Icon-style Moses and Aaron in the left foreground with plain gold halos, pig rooting at center and a pillar of cloud (no face or figure) over the tabernacle at top center; painted to all four edges. Aaron's white headband (upper left-center, at his brow) carries a dark glyph-like script mark at its center, which counts as an inscription.

Watercolor: kneeling mother and child reaching toward rays breaking through clouds above a terraced village, boats on the lake at left, Roman soldier, wood-carrying villagers and grain basket at right. Bottom-left corner and parts of the left edge fade softly into white paper (style fade, not a flaw); no lettering in corners or sky.

Haloed Boaz stands at left with staff facing a lit doorway (plain halo, no marks; shawl hem has only geometric weave), but an unrequested young woman in a yellow veil kneels at center-right lighting the lamps and would read as Ruth or Naomi though only Boaz is in the scene's cast. All four edges are painted through; no lettering found.

Icon-style Jericho: haloed priests in linen and violet blow long horns at right, haloed Joshua with spear at center, Israelite crowd climbing the rubble of the collapsed central wall into the city, tents at left; halos are plain gold, painting reaches all four edges. Only a tiny sprig-like ornament on a building wall at upper right (no lettering); one priest second from right holds no horn, a minor slip.

The central woman wears a red maphorion with the three Theotokos stars on forehead and shoulders and holds a child's hand while a bent old man with a staff reaches toward him (center), so the group reads as Mary, the Christ child and Simeon (a Presentation icon) rather than anonymous villagers. Most onlookers face the viewer instead of the doorway, and no reading is shown; the edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Oil painting: Jesus at right with arm raised and mouth open calling toward the rock tomb at center-left, the stone rolled aside; Lazarus in grave wrappings with face cloth steps out of the dark doorway, a kneeling woman (Martha) at front-left and a crowd around. Paint reaches all four borders, and the corners and sky show no lettering.

A seated mother and a child raising a hand toward light rays breaking from overcast clouds (center-left), with a basket of grain, bundled wood, boats on the lake and a red-cloaked Roman soldier on the road at right; the clouds hold only light, no figure. The town is a larger walled city with a domed building rather than a village, a minor departure; edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Ezekiel stands center-left in a side view with an open palm toward a valley of scattered skeletons, with dust blowing at right. The sky is cloudy rather than pale and even, but no figure appears in the clouds, and all corners are clean.

Jonah half-submerged at left beside the great fish's glowing open mouth (glow only, no divine figure), sailors on the ship at right; painted to all edges. On the ship (upper right, behind the rail ropes left of the seated sailor) one sailor in a grey tunic has arms gripping the rail and rope but no head, a malformed figure.

Icon: haloed Job with staff stands in front of (not on) the ash heap under a dark cloud whirlwind with radiance breaking through at top center; no face or figure in the storm, halo is plain gold. Job looks forward rather than up at the storm and the walled towns behind are intact rather than ruined; all four edges painted, no lettering.

Moses with staff at left foreground and a long column of families carrying children cross a rocky path between waves; God appears only as a distant flame pillar at center horizon and fire glints in the right water wall, no face or figure. Sky is a gold daytime ground rather than night, and the left side is low open sea with a wall only in the distance; edges full, no text.

Watercolor of a dark, empty sea with pale radiance breaking from the top center and mist wisps over the water; God appears only as light, no face or silhouette in the glow or mist. Wash reaches all four borders with no blank paper band or writing in the corners.
A raised gold icon-board border frames the painting on all four sides. Inside, David reclines with his staff beside a still pool, with sheep and a hill village; his plain gold halo has no marks.

Empty golden throne at center under a rainbow with cloud and lightning, with no figure or face on it; four winged creatures (lion, ox, winged man, eagle) with eyes on their wings and bodies stand on a glassy reflecting floor, and empty elder thrones line both sides. The creatures stand in a row before the throne rather than ringing it, and there is an unrequested gold chest before the steps; the wall panels and cloth ornaments are abstract, with no lettering.

Fiery sulfur streaks and debris rain from a burning sky onto a mud-brick city in the valley (left-center), with smoke columns, a river and the sun low on the right hills; the fire contains no face or figure. Only one distinct city cluster reads clearly (the right side shows burning cracked ground), but there are no people, the edges are fully painted, and there is no lettering.

Icon-style haloed child stands at center with a wolf and lamb at left and a leopard, goat, calf and lion at right. A shepherd's staff lies in the foreground and a walled town sits upper left. The plain gold halo has no marks. A Byzantine domed chapel at right is a minor anachronism with no cross or lettering.

Classical oil painting: white-bearded old man lying on his back with eyes closed and hands folded at center-right, two kneeling and two standing mourners beside him, well, huts, tools, jar and sheep; all four edges painted, no lettering in corners. He lies on his back rather than his side and mourners are grouped rather than at the frame edges, minor deviations.

Icon: still, glassy pale water ringed by ochre-and-red hills under a gold-leaf sky with a low band of cloud at the horizon; unpeopled. Paint reaches all four edges; small dark marks near bottom center are grass tufts, not lettering.

Job with staff stands upright on a grey ash heap at center looking up into a swirling dust whirlwind with bright light breaking through the storm; zoomed whirlwind, bright area and cloud corners show no face or figure. Painting runs to all four borders and no lettering is present; the town at right looks intact rather than ruined, a minor detail.

Classical scene with broken mudbrick walls, Joshua with spear at center and white-turbaned priests blowing shofars while carrying the ark at right, no lettering and full edges. But the column in the wall gap and the foreground crowd run toward the viewer, out of the city and away from it, so the verse's key action (going up into the city) is reversed.

The throne is empty, with radiance, a green rainbow arc, lightning and cloud (center), so God has no figure. Lion, ox, man and eagle creatures with eyed wings stand around it on a glassy floor, with a few elder thrones at the side edges; the wall bands are vine ornament with no glyphs, and the painting reaches all four edges.

Ink and watercolor: Job with a staff stands on a grey ash heap with broken pottery, looking up at a spiralling dust whirlwind whose bright center is only light and swirl lines, with no face or form. The paint and ink reach all four edges (the pale left-edge sky is a painted wash, not a margin), and there are no marks in the corners.

The Shulammite stands left of center under a blossoming apple tree holding wildflowers and a basket, with wild roses (lower left), lilies (lower right), vineyards and a hill village behind; no shepherd appears. The shepherd's staff (center) stands upright on its own in the grass rather than leaning on a tree, a minor oddity; edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

In ink and watercolor, Abraham stands at center-right with the knife raised in his right hand and his face turned to the dawn sky. Isaac lies bound on wood stacked on a stone altar, with a single tree at right and the valley behind. God appears only as warm sky light, with no form. The sky wash fades to white paper along the upper-left edge, which is style-consistent.

Two walled mud-brick cities burning under streaks of falling fire, smoke clouds with no face or figure in the sky. A raised gilded frame border runs around all four sides of the painting, framing the scene as an icon panel.

Watercolor: Jesus stands at the left end of the boat with arm outstretched over breaking waves while nine disciples grip the rail and rigging, torn sail and lantern present; light is overcast day rather than night/dawn. All four corners and the left edge fade into white paper (style fade); fringe marks at right edge are cloak tassels, not lettering.

About ten exiles sit on the grass in the foreground with heads bowed and hands clasped, a river and willows behind and walled Babylon with ziggurats on the far bank at dusk. Lyres and a lute lie on the grass at lower left and lower right, still strung rather than unstrung (minor); all four edges painted through and no lettering on walls or instruments.

Icon-style: haloed Saul kneels at center shielding his eyes under a broad shaft of light with plain concentric arcs at top (no figure in the light), six companions shield their eyes, Damascus at upper right; halos plain, edges full. Minor issues: two unnamed companions at left wear halos, the city has an anachronistic minaret and domes, and a few faint pale marks on the city wall are visible only at heavy zoom.

The sea is not divided: one huge breaking wave stands at the left, and the channel beyond it is still filled with flowing water, with no second wall and no dry sea floor, so Moses (left foreground) seems to gesture at an incoming wave. Yahweh appears only as a bright break in the dark clouds (top center), with no figure; the painting reaches all edges and there is no lettering.

Icon-style: haloed Daniel stands centered in a round stone den with four calm, closed-mouthed lions, under a beam of light from above that has no angel or divine figure in it; Darius leans in at the upper-left rim by an iron grille and wooden lid. Both halos are plain gold with no marks, and the gold ground reaches all edges. A small unrequested bearded onlooker peers over the wall in the top-left corner, and Darius oddly has a halo.

At the top center, above the rainbow, a faint robed human figure with head, shoulders and arms is painted into the light and clouds, standing for God over the empty throne. Otherwise the four eyed, haloed creatures (lion, ox, man, eagle) stand on a glassy sea before the throne with side thrones, plain halos, no lettering, and gold ground reaching all edges.

A painted gold panel border with a raised inner molding frames all four sides of the icon, which is a frame flaw. Inside it, priests blow horns before a breached Jericho wall, Joshua stands with sword and spear, people shout at left and stream through the gap, and the Ark is carried at right. No lettering is visible.

David in a blue robe reclines on the grass in the lower right beside a still pool at left, holding a shepherd's crook, with lyre and sword beside him, sheep grazing and resting, hill villages and a rising sun. Painted to all four edges, no lettering in corners or on the lyre.

Watercolor: Jesus in front of the rolled-back stone calls out with arm raised skyward while linen-wrapped Lazarus walks out of the dark tomb at center-left; Martha in green with clasped hands and a crowd fill the foreground. Jesus faces the viewer rather than the tomb; the pale sky at top right is a painted wash reaching the edge; no lettering.

David at left center still holds the stone in his sling pouch while Goliath at center right is already toppling, so the stone never reaches the forehead; Goliath's body is contorted upside down with his face inverted at the bottom and his spear has blades at both ends. Edges are painted through and no lettering appears; Philistine and Israelite ranks flank the scene as requested.

Ink-and-watercolor: a small child with a shepherd's crook rests a hand on a wolf lying beside a lamb, leopard with goat and calf with a lion at right, terraced Judean hills and walled town behind. The wash fades softly to white paper in the pale sky and the lower-left corner (style-consistent); no lettering, though the lion is a full-maned adult.

The concubine (lower right) has her eyes wide open and looks up alertly, so she reads as a living woman about to be stabbed rather than a still body. The night interior also opens through a broken wall onto a flat gold sky (top center). The edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

A painted signature ('Tgalali') sits in the bottom-right corner, and behind the parted sanctuary curtain (center, below the right seraph's feet) a faint bearded, robed figure with a reaching hand is visible. The two bronze seraphim hide their faces with hands and wings but show four wings each and bare uncovered feet, above Isaiah with a staff at left.

Goliath (right) is flipped upside down with legs straight up in the air, crashing onto his helmeted head and back with his face toward the viewer, which contradicts falling forward on his face after a forehead strike; he is also barely larger than David. David (left) follows through with the sling, armies line both hillsides, the white patch at top center is a painted sun glow rather than a margin, and shields carry no lettering.

A painted gold panel border frames all four sides, which is a frame flaw. Inside, men and veiled women sit grieving with heads in their hands on a riverbank, Babylon's walls and ziggurats sit on the far shore, and two lyres hang in a willow at upper left rather than resting on the ground. No lettering is visible.

A raised gilded frame border surrounds the whole icon. Moses (left of center, plain gold halo) stretches his arm toward the Israelites at left rather than over the sea, the sea is parted into two curling walls with a dry path, and light rays break from the clouds at top with no figure.

Icon: Isaiah looks up from lower center at two winged seraphim above swirling incense smoke in a columned temple; no figure or face in the smoke or sanctuary. Seraphim show about four wings with bare feet uncovered, the left one holds tongs with a burning coal (from v.6), and Isaiah oddly grips two separate staffs; gold ground reaches all edges.

A raised gold ornamental border frames the whole panel on all four sides. Haloed Moses at left stretches his hand over a sea split into two cliffs of water with wind-blown sand, God shown only as a cloud with light rays at top center (no face or figure), but the scene is a daytime gold ground rather than night and every Israelite wears a plain halo.

Icon-style Ezekiel stands among skulls and bones with one hand outstretched, God shown nowhere (only wind swirls in a plain gold sky). The landscape is inset, leaving a plain gold border band about 25px wide down the full left and right edges; he also holds a blank wooden tablet and writes with a stylus instead of only speaking to the bones.

Goliath (center right) falls backward rather than on his face. He still wears a helmet while a second, duplicate helmet flies off his head, and the stone bounces away above him instead of sinking into his forehead. Both armies wear identical red-crested Greek hoplite kit; the edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Saul at center lurches mid-stride with both hands raised against a broad shaft of light from the clouds; the shaft is pure light with no figure in it. Companions crouch and shield their eyes with dropped staffs around him, and walled Damascus sits in the left background; the paint reaches all four edges with no corner marks.

Jesus' cruciform halo on the cross (top center) has small glyph-like marks painted in its arms. He is also still fully dressed in a white tunic and the same blue-grey mantle that lies on the ground being divided (bottom center), contradicting the dividing of his clothing; otherwise soldiers kneel in a circle with one raising a lot, onlookers stand on the road at right, and gold ground and rocks reach all edges.

Four Roman soldiers crouch around garments in the foreground, one raising a stick-like lot, while the crucified Jesus stands on the cross at upper right with onlookers on the road at left. The titulus board atop the cross carries faint grey glyph-like marks. In this ink-and-watercolor image the paper fades to white along the left and bottom edges.

Bald, bearded Elisha in a fur mantle walks the rocky road at center-left while six boys at right by the town gate jeer and point (one scoops dust), with a walled town and golden calf shrine on the hilltop; painted to all edges, no lettering. He walks toward the viewer, away from the gate and without looking at the mockers, instead of heading up toward the town.

Watercolor: streaks of burning sulfur fall from a smoky sky onto a walled mud-brick city on a palm-dotted plain, with small fires in the fields and dawn glow on the right horizon; no figure or face in the clouds (Yahweh shown only as fire from the sky). One main city rather than two is clearly shown; the bottom-left corner and parts of the left edge fade softly into paper (style fade); no lettering.

Peter at center leaps from the boat over the shallows clutching a rough cloak around himself, the beloved disciple stands in the boat at right pointing toward the shore, and Jesus stands small at left by a charcoal fire in morning mist. All four edges are painted through (pale sky glow at top left still textured paint) and no lettering anywhere.

Icon-style boat with Jesus standing at the stern holding out his hand over calming water and disciples looking up, but a raised gold frame surrounds all four sides. Jesus's cross-nimbus at upper right carries Greek letters in its arms; an oil lamp also hangs oddly on the outside of the hull.

This is an unpeopled ink-and-watercolor landscape: still, glassy water between low ochre hills under a pale dawn sky, with soft fades to white paper at the left edge and the upper corners. It reads more like an ordinary calm lake than a radiant renewed earth whose sea is gone, and the small ink ticks on the lower-right hillside are grass, not lettering.

The anonymous mother and child are painted as a Virgin-and-Christ-Child icon (left-center): the mother has a gold halo with star-marked veil, and the child has a cruciform halo inscribed with letters (O / O / N-like glyphs) in its arms. The village, lake boats, grain basket, wood-carriers and Roman soldier match, but the child does not lift a hand to the light; the gold sky break shows only rays.

Abraham (center) raises a curved knife in his right hand with his face turned upward, his left hand on Isaac, who lies bound with rope on stacked wood over a fieldstone altar on a ridge with a single tree at left and a valley at right. Both halos are plain outlined circles with no marks, the gold sky holds no figure, and painting reaches all edges.

Villagers, women with children and one holding a child's hand, stand facing the open doorway of a stone building at right where a veiled figure waits. A Roman soldier walks behind at left, with water jars and palms around. The lunette over the door is interlaced lattice ornament, not lettering, and the corners are clean. The walls are bare stone rather than whitewashed, and the group stands in a line rather than a half-circle.

Solid dark-red painted border bands with a thin cream inner line run down the full left and right edges. The two seraphim (top) have four wings and uncovered faces and bare feet, and the left one holds tongs with a burning coal, the action of a later verse. Isaiah stands at right before smoke and radiance with no divine figure.

Watercolor: Peter clutches his cloak mid-leap over a splash between the boat (right, with the beloved disciple pointing and a net and oar) and Jesus standing by a charcoal fire on the stony shore (left) at dawn. Jesus is near rather than small in the distance; the top and left edges fade into white paper (style fade); hatching on the bottom-left rock is shading, not lettering.

Abraham stands at center left with the knife raised in his right hand and face lifted, beside a stone altar where Isaac lies roped on stacked wood, on a ridge above a deep valley with one tree at right. Sky at upper right holds only sun rays and cloud, no figure; edges painted through and no lettering.

Painterly night scene: Peter steps off the boat's side, one foot on the gunwale and one on the waves, reaching toward a softly glowing Jesus standing on the water at right center, with disciples and an oil lamp in the boat at left under stormy moonlit clouds. Edges full and no lettering; a coiled net hangs oddly from a pole across Peter's hip and Jesus's hem sits in the swell, both minor.

Balding Elisha, with a plain outline halo and a hair mantle (left), walks along the road while seven youths at the town gate (right) point and laugh, and a golden calf on a plinth stands on the rise. He walks down and away from the town rather than up toward it. The tiny relief on the small altar is ornament, not lettering, and the painting reaches all four edges.

At night a long column of Israelite families carrying children and bundles walks between towering curling walls of sea, while Moses with a staff stands at front-left, arm lowered. A pillar of fire at the far end of the path is pure flame with no figure; the 'dry ground' looks wet and stony, and there are no corner marks.

David (plain-halo, center-left) reclines on green grass beside a still pond, holding his staff and gazing at the water, with sheep grazing and lying on both sides and hill villages behind; no divine figure appears in the gold sky. Unrequested props (harp at lower left, sheathed sword) and a second loose stick by his feet (lower right) are minor; there is no lettering and painting reaches all edges.

Daniel stands calm at center of a circular stone den with closed-mouthed lions lying around him. Darius in a purple robe and crown leans over the rim at upper right, beside a barred wooden lid at upper left. The angel and God appear only as a soft beam of light at top center, with no figure in it. Daniel's satchel and all corners are free of marks.

The icon of the Shulammite holding wildflowers (plain gold halo, lilies, roses, flowering tree, a crook standing in the field) is a square panel occupying only the center. The left and right quarters of the frame are blurred pillarbox fill rather than painting, so neither side edge is painted.

Icon: the haloed Shulammite in red veil holds roses and lilies beside a blossoming tree, a leaning shepherd's staff and vineyards, matching the scene. But the painting is a narrow vertical panel set on wide blank gold bands filling the left (x 0-380) and right (x 985-1376) of the frame; halo and robe ornaments contain no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor courtyard with whitewashed walls, stone arch, palm and jars; a robed reader holds a blank open book in the dark doorway at left while a line of villagers and a child holding a woman's hand stand mostly facing the viewer rather than toward the doorway, with two Roman soldiers (one at left beside the elder) rather than a background tunic. Left and bottom edges fade to white paper, which is the style; no lettering found on the book or corners.

Ink-and-watercolor: the Shulammite stands left of center holding roses and lilies among wild roses and lilies, with a blossoming tree, a vineyard and a hill town behind; she is alone and the wash reaches all four edges. The shepherd's staff stands upright on its own in the meadow instead of leaning on a tree; a squiggle in the grass hatching at the right edge looks glyph-like only at heavy zoom.

Priests in blue and white (right) blow trumpets beside collapsed, dusty mudbrick walls, with Joshua holding a spear and sword (center) and tents at the left. Most of the crowd walks toward the viewer rather than into the city, and the bottom edge and corners fade to white paper in watercolor style; the ink strokes on the right wall are texture, not lettering.

Ink and watercolor night interior: a grim grey-haired man in a grey cloak kneels with a raised knife beside the still woman lying on a mat, with no gore shown; an oil lamp on a stool is at right and a saddled donkey stands in the dark doorway behind. The wash reaches all four borders, and there are no marks in the corners or on the floor.

Nine Israelite exiles sit on the riverbank (foreground) with bowed heads and hands to faces, with lyres and bundles on the ground and Babylon's walls and ziggurat across the water at dusk; the lyres are still strung and palms stand in for willows, both minor. The only edge issue is a tiny fleck of unpainted white paper at the extreme bottom-right corner, consistent with the ink-and-watercolor style; there is no lettering.

Saul walks at center shielding his eyes under a blaze of rays from above, flanked by four companions with staffs and satchels shielding their faces, with Damascus behind. The light holds no figure. Loopy ink pebble squiggles are scattered across the road, and one at lower left near (20,660) looks faintly cursive but matches the ground texture everywhere else. The watercolor sky fades to white paper at the top and upper-right edges.

Ink-and-watercolor: bald, bearded Elisha in a fur-collared mantle at left, four youths jeering and pointing on the road at center-right, with a golden calf on a pedestal and the walled town with its gate above. The wash fades to white paper along the top-left sky and the bottom-right corner, consistent with the style. As in the scene's other render, Elisha walks toward the viewer, away from the gate.

Icon: Peter clutching his cloak leaps from the boat over rippling water while the beloved disciple points from the boat (left) and a small Jesus stands by a charcoal fire on the shore (right), matching the scene. But the painted scene is inset inside a plain gold border band about 25-30px wide on the left, right and bottom edges, ruled off by a dark line; no lettering.

The grey-haired father in a swinging brown cloak embraces the ragged, barefoot-sandalled son around the neck at center on a stony village road, with hands and arms resolving plausibly, a winding road, terraced hills and village behind. A colonnaded Greek-style temple at center right is an odd background detail; edges painted through and no lettering.

Grey-bearded father in ochre robe and flying red cloak, mid-stride, embraces the young travel-worn son around the neck on a stone road at center; walled farmhouse with gate at left, terraced hills and lake behind. Only a soft watercolor fade to white paper along the lower left edge; no lettering found in corners, buildings or boats.

In this gold-ground icon, an old white-bearded man lies dead on a rock slab (center) with eleven unhaloed mourners kneeling and standing around him. A stone well and jar sit at the left, crossed hoes and a sickle lie in the foreground, and sheep and a domed village fill the background. He lies on his back rather than his side, the mourners are more than a few, and there are no halos, lettering or border.

A raised gold-leaf icon frame borders all four sides as a painted panel edge. Inside, nine grieving exiles sit with heads in hands on the grassy bank in the foreground, harps lie on the ground, and walled Babylon with ziggurats lines the far side of the river under a gold sky with a red dusk horizon; the corners and frame show no lettering.

White-bearded robed elders sit on the side thrones at far left and far right, adding the unselected twenty-four elders; the man-faced creature (center-right) is a robed man on human feet with a spotted animal body, hooves and tail behind him, an awkward hybrid. The throne is empty with only rainbow, lightning and light (no divine figure), the eyed lion, ox and eagle stand before a glassy sea, edges are fully painted, and there is no lettering.

An unpeopled luminous landscape shows a still, glassy lake winding through flowering hills and rocks, under a radiant pale sky with faint cloud at the horizon. The sky holds no face or figure, and the corners are clean.

Four crouching Roman soldiers around garments on the ground in the foreground, one raising his hand, with a crucified Christ on the hilltop at upper left, Jerusalem's walls at right and four distant onlookers on the road; painted to all edges. The tiny plaque atop the cross (upper left) is a pale blank board with no legible or glyph-like lettering at zoom.

Watercolor: bearded Ezekiel in a brown cloak stands center-left with his hand outstretched over a valley strewn with skulls and bones; God appears only as voice (no figure). He oddly holds a blank wooden writing tablet and stylus that read like a clipboard and pencil, which the scene did not ask for; all edges fade softly into white paper (style fade); the tablet is blank, with no lettering.

Daniel stands calm at center among six sleeping lions with closed mouths, Darius in purple robes and signet ring leans over the den rim at upper left, and a soft warm glow above Daniel's head stands for the angel with no figure in it. The den reads shallow (rim near Daniel's head height) and the lid and gate are absent, but nothing contradictory; edges painted through, no lettering.

Grim bearded Levite in grey cloak kneels center-right with a knife raised over the still, fully clothed concubine lying on a mat, lit by a small oil lamp; moonlit window upper left and a saddled donkey in the doorway at right. Painting reaches all edges, no lettering; only nit is a stirruped, modern-looking saddle on the donkey.

Jesus (right) stands ankle-deep in the water just off a reedy shore with a village close behind, so he reads as wading in shallows rather than walking on the open sea. Peter steps barefoot from the boat (left) while oddly holding a staff, and the disciples and lamp sit in the boat; the edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Jesus' cruciform halo (top center) is inscribed with the letters O / θ / N, and a raised gold-leaf frame borders all four edges. The scene otherwise fits: Jesus stands with arm outstretched in a boat of twelve disciples under a torn sail, waves at left give way to calm rings at right, and an oil lamp hangs oddly on the outside of the hull.

A painted gold border frames the image on all four sides. A small painted monogram or signature sits in the waves at the bottom-right corner, and Jesus' halo (right) carries cross arms with glyph-like marks. The scene itself fits: Peter steps off the boat's bow toward a small radiant Jesus standing on the waves, with the disciples and a lamp in the boat under a stormy moonlit sky.

Moses with a staff and Aaron stand side by side in the foreground, with a pig rooting in straw at right, Israelites at a distance among tents, and the tabernacle at center. A column of smoke above the tabernacle holds no figure or face. Aaron wears a high-priest ephod with a plain-stone breastplate instead of plain linen; the stones and his headband carry no marks.

Boaz with staff and blue mantle stands at left in a mud-brick courtyard with jars, bench and an open doorway at right; painted to all edges, no lettering. A young headscarfed woman kneels lighting a clay lamp at the doorway (right-center); she is unnamed and the scene does call for lamps being lit, but beside Boaz at Naomi's house she reads as Ruth, who the plan left out.

Dark oil-style painting of a stormy night: a huge fish rises with jaws agape just behind waist-deep Jonah (center-right), and sailors line the rail of the ship at upper left under lightning; a faint misty glow at upper right holds no face or figure. Jonah faces away from the mouth, so he reads as about to be swallowed rather than being taken in, and odd branch-like seaweed floats at the bottom; paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Jesus at right center wears a cross nimbus inscribed with Greek letters O, Ω/O and N in its arms, clearly legible lettering inside the halo. Otherwise the scene matches: linen-wrapped haloed Lazarus steps from a dark rock tomb beside its rolled stone at center left, mourners flank both sides with a veiled Martha at front right, and edges are painted through.

Icon-style panel: the grey-haired father in brown robe and red cloak strides forward and embraces the barefoot, ragged son around the neck on a dirt road at center, with a walled farmstead and gate at left, terraced hills and a lake with boats at right. Gold sky runs to every edge with no border band; both men wear plain unmarked outline halos (unusual for parable figures but not lettering).

The white-haired man lies with his eyes closed and his head on a bundle at center. Three relatives stand and four kneel around him, with the stone well, jar and tools at right, black tents and mud-brick houses behind, and sheep at left; the wash reaches all four borders, with only tiny pale specks at the left and right edges, and no lettering in the corners or on any object.

Oil painting from the bow: Jesus stands on the raised stern deck with arm outstretched under parting storm clouds, with about twelve disciples seated along both gunwales turned toward him, a torn sail at upper right and a lit oil lamp on the deck. The sea is still choppy at the sides, and the paint reaches all four edges with no corner marks.

A stylized radiant semicircle of concentric gold and pale bands with rays rises at the horizon (center) over a dark, empty, wave-patterned deep with drifting mist, with no land and no face or figure in the light. The light reads somewhat like a sunrise from the horizon rather than radiance from above, and the gold-leaf sky is bright rather than dark, both minor; gold and dark water reach all edges with no lettering.

A long column of Israelite families carrying children, with a sheep and a dog, walks the dry seabed between towering water walls. Moses stands with his staff and lowered arm at front right. God appears only as an orange fire plume in the dark sky at top center, with no face or figure in it. The corners and edges are clean and painted.

Ink-and-watercolor: Boaz with a crook staff and blue mantle stands at left in a mud-brick courtyard, with an open doorway, benches, a jar and a burning lamp at right; the wash reaches all four edges and there is no lettering. A young headscarfed woman crouches lighting a lamp at the doorway (right-center); she is unnamed and the scene calls for lamps being lit, but at Naomi's house she reads as Ruth, who the plan left out.

Icon: haloed Peter steps from the boat's edge toward a glowing Jesus standing on the waves at right, with eleven haloed disciples, a net and an oil lamp in the boat (the sky is gold leaf rather than night). Jesus' cross-halo at upper right carries Greek-style letters (O, ω and N) in its arms; paint reaches all four edges.

Dark rolling waters fill the lower frame with a pale radiance breaking through mist at upper left and wisps of mist drifting right; brightened crops of the light and the mist wisps show no face, hands or human silhouette. Edges are painted dark sea and sky to all four borders (right edge slightly darker, no band) and there is no lettering.

A painted gold border band (with a thin light inner rule) runs down the full left and right edges and across the top, framing the icon. Otherwise the scene matches: a column of Israelite families with children and bundles walks between blue water walls toward the far shore, a haloed Moses with staff stands at right, and God's presence is shown only as flame columns inside the water walls with no face or figure; the only lettering-like mark is a faint ~15px squiggle on the ground between feet at bottom-left center, which reads as ground texture.

David reclines on the grass holding his staff beside a still pool, with sheep, an early sun and a village on the hills, and no figure for the 'He' of the verse. In the lower-left grass beside the lyre (about x60, y575) is a small, isolated ink mark that reads as the initials 'JR'; separately, at the top-right corner the blue sky wash stops short of the right border and leaves pale paper there (a watercolor fade).

Moses at left holds his staff out over a stormy sea while the Israelites crowd the beach at right under a glowing cloud with no figure in it. The sea is not divided: there are no walls of water and no dry path, only surf breaking on a shore with exposed seabed rocks in the foreground, so the verse's central event is missing. There is no lettering and no margin.

A small child stands at center among resting animals: a wolf with a lamb (left), a leopard beside a young goat, a calf and a young lion (right), with a shepherd's staff on the ground in the foreground and a terraced Judean village and stone gate behind. The child stands rather than actively leading and only one calf appears, both minor; no Isaiah appears, edges are fully painted, and there is no lettering.

Icon-style haloed Jonah stands waist-deep in waves at center, reaching up to a huge fish whose open mouth glows inside. Sailors haul ropes in the ship at upper left under swirling clouds and lightning on gold. The plain halo has no marks, and God appears only as the glow, with no figure. The bottom fifth is stylized seaweed scrollwork, but it is the underwater zone, overlapped by Jonah's robe and the fish, rather than a border band.

Ink-and-watercolor: bald, white-bearded Moses with a staff and Aaron in an ephod and twelve-stone breastplate (plain headband, no marks) stand side by side at left, a pig roots at center, men and women watch at right, and a smoke column with no figure rises over the tabernacle. The wash fades to white paper at the bottom-left and upper-right edges, consistent with the style.

Icon: linen-bound Lazarus stands at the mouth of a rock tomb with its round stone (left) as Jesus raises his arm toward him, with a veiled Martha and a crowd at right. The whole picture sits inside a raised gold frame running around all four edges, and Jesus' cross-halo has letters (O, O, IB-like glyphs) in its arms.

Two bronze-toned winged seraphim hover over Isaiah, faces veiled by a wing or hands, but both have bare feet dangling uncovered beneath their robes, contrary to the verse, and the left seraph holds tongs with a burning coal from a later verse. The bright glow at top center is only light and incense smoke with no figure; the cherub carvings on the gold door lintel are temple ornament, edges are painted through and no lettering appears.

A raised gold frame, about 35px wide, surrounds all four edges of the icon, and Jesus' cross-nimbus (upper right) has an 'O' glyph painted in each of its three arms. The scene itself matches: the haloed beloved disciple points from the boat at left, Peter clutches his cloak mid-leap into the surf at center, and Jesus stands on the shore by a charcoal fire at right; no corner signatures.

A wide, thick gold-leaf border with a recessed inner edge runs around all four sides, so the picture is set inside a painted frame. Inside it, zigzag fire bolts and fireballs fall from a gold sky onto a walled city and a smaller second city, with smoke, the sun over the eastern hills and no people; God appears only as the fire from the sky, with no face or figure in it, and there is no lettering on the border or in the scene.
